query: Classify each user_review into exactly one of these five product areas: Search & Navigation, Performance & Speed, Reliability & Stability, User Interface, Customer Support. Save all rows with a new product_area column to result.csv.

Identify the primary intent of each customer_notes row as exactly one of: Complaint, Inquiry, Refund Request, Suggestion, Praise. A note may express urgency or emotion, but the intent label must capture what the customer wants to happen. Save all rows with a new intent column to result.csv.

Find the user_review rows that neither praise the product's core functionality nor request any change or fix (for example pure usage descriptions, comparisons with other tools, or remarks about the reviewer's own workflow). Add a matches_filter column with Yes or No for every row, save all rows to result.csv, and save only the matching rows to filtered.csv.

From each review, extract the specific product feature points the reviewer mentions (open set, not from a predefined list) as a semicolon-separated list in a new feature_points column. Use NONE when no concrete feature is mentioned. Save all rows to result.csv.

Identify the distinct problem topics raised in the support_ticket column, counting different wordings of the same underlying problem as one topic. Produce topic_counts.csv with columns topic, description, count sorted by count descending, and result.csv with every original row plus its assigned topic.

Consider only the orders whose ReturnStatus is Returned. Summarize the common themes in their customer_reason texts. Produce themes.csv with columns theme, description, count covering the returned subset, and result.csv marking every original row with in_subset (Yes/No) and, for subset rows, the assigned theme.

Score every customer_comment on an explicitly anchored 1-10 actionability scale: 1 means nothing for the business to act on, 10 means a concrete, specific, immediately actionable request or problem report. Emotional intensity alone must not raise the score. Sort all rows by actionability descending and save them with the actionability column to result.csv.

Score every description row on an explicitly anchored 1-10 information-density scale, where 1 means vague marketing language with no concrete details and 10 means many specific verifiable details (numbers, materials, dimensions, named technologies). Sort all rows by info_density descending and save them with the info_density column to result.csv.

For each feedback row, produce between 3 and 5 keywords that capture its most distinctive content, as a semicolon-separated list in a new tags column. Keywords must be words or short phrases actually grounded in the row's text, not generic labels. Save all rows to result.csv.

Cluster the customer_feedback column into coherent semantic groups, but put clearly outlying entries (semantically unrelated to every other group) into a dedicated group named Outliers instead of forcing them into a regular group. Produce groups.csv with columns group_name, description, count, and result.csv with every original row plus its group_name.

Some product_defect entries describe the same underlying defect in different wording. Assign every row a dup_group identifier (D01, D02, ...) so that rows describing the same defect share one identifier, and rows describing a defect no other row mentions get their own singleton identifier. Save all rows with dup_group to result.csv.

Find the email_body rows that refer to the competitor company Nexora Technologies, including indirect references through abbreviations, product names, or misspellings. Add a mentions_competitor column with Yes or No for every row and save all rows to result.csv. Be careful not to flag other similarly named companies.

From each meeting_record, extract the committed budget amount into amount_usd (a plain number in US dollars, no separators or currency symbols) and the agreed delivery date into delivery_date (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD). Use NONE where a field is not stated. Save all rows with both columns to result.csv.

From each project_log entry, extract who is currently responsible for the task into owner and what the task is into task. Pay attention to reassignments and suggestions: the owner is the person who actually holds the task after the events described, not merely the first name mentioned. Save all rows with owner and task to result.csv.

Convert each free-form candidate_profile into structured columns: full_name, years_experience (integer), primary_skill, city. Leave a cell empty when the profile genuinely does not state that field. Save all rows with the four new columns to result.csv.

Using subject and body together, classify each email into exactly one of: Billing Issue, Technical Problem, Account Access, Feature Request, General Inquiry. When subject and body disagree, the body content decides. Save all rows with a new category column to result.csv.

The catalog table lists products with product_id and product_name. For each order in the orders table, match its free-text item_description to the correct catalog product and write that product_id into a matched_product_id column; leave it blank when no catalog product matches. Save all order rows with matched_product_id to result.csv.

Review the spec_note column for likely data-entry errors such as impossible magnitudes, wrong units, or values inconsistent with the product category. Add is_suspect (Yes/No) and, for suspect rows, a short suggested_fix describing the likely correction. Save all rows to result.csv.

Rewrite each product_name into the canonical format 'Brand Model Variant' with exactly one space between tokens: brand first with initial capital, model code in upper case, variant (when present) capitalized, dropping parenthetical remarks, edition suffixes, and seller boilerplate. Keep the original column and add canonical_name. Save all rows to result.csv.
